description.content: APIs for importing accounts.

item.name: Use this endpoint to stage account data before creating an account.

request.name: Use this endpoint to stage account data before creating an account.

description.content: As the name suggests, this endpoint stores the data in Kraken but does not create an account from the data. Staged account data can be updated as many times as you like before an account is created.

response.name: If the payload is valid, **and the request is updating data for an account that has been staged previously**, then a `200 OK` response will be returned detailing the `external_account_number` and `import_supplier`.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

response.name: If the payload is valid, **and the request is staging data for an account for the first time**, then a `201 Created` response will be returned detailing the `external_account_number` and `import_supplier`.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

response.name:
If account data fails to be staged, then the details of the validation errors will
be returned in the response. In this scenario, check that:
- The payload is valid (refer to the field definitions and validation rules table).
- The account has not been imported already, or marked to be skipped.
- The migration for the `import_supplier` is still ongoing (if you receive an error
  indicating it is paused or complete, get in touch with the Kraken team).

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

item.name: Use this endpoint to process staged account data into an account in Kraken.

request.name: Use this endpoint to process staged account data into an account in Kraken.

description.content: The endpoint accepts a JSON payload that contains an object referencing existing staged account data. The `operations_team_name` that the account should be linked to should also be provided. An optional `dry_run` field is available to test the account creation process without actually creating the account. This is useful for testing the process to ensure that an account would be created successfully.

response.name: If the payload is valid and an account has been created, the newly created Kraken account number will be returned in the response.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

response.name:
If there are validation errors, they will be detailed in the body of the response.
To resolve these errors, refer to the field definitions and validation rules.

If an account has already been imported then two additional fields will be present
in the response: `external_account_number` and `kraken_account_number`.

If the API request was run with the `dry_run` flag set to `true`, and the request
would ordinarily have been successful, then the response will also be returned.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

item.name: Use this endpoint to add notes to an account.

request.name: Use this endpoint to add notes to an account.

description.content:
Some points to note:
- A note must contain at least one of the fields `body` or `document_paths`.
- A `created_at` datetime may optionally be provided. Otherwise, it will default to the current local time.
- The `document_paths` refer to the locations in S3 where attached documents are stored.
- An optional `is_pinned` boolean can be passed in the payload to control whether this note will be pinned to the top of the Kraken account support site page.

response.name: If the payload is valid, a list of the posted notes and their creation status will be returned in the response. A new note will only be created if a note on the account with the same body (and `created_at`, if provided) does not already exist.

item.name: Use this endpoint to import financial transactions to an account.

request.name: Use this endpoint to import financial transactions to an account.

description.content: Use this endpoint to import financial transactions to an account.

query.description: Boolean flag indicating whether to check if a transaction has already been added.

boolean flag. If set to true and the payload contains a transaction that is outside the currently-open statement period, this will modify the transaction date so that it is within the currently-open statement period. This then allows the transaction to be added to the statement instead of throwing an error. A description is added to the transaction to explain this, and a note is pinned to the account.

body.raw:
{
  "import_supplier": "<string>",
  "account_number": "<string>",
  "dry_run": false,
  "external_account_number": "<string>",
  "transactions": [
    {
      "amount": "<decimal>",
      "transaction_date": "<date>",
      "transaction_id": "<string>",
      "type": "<string>",
      "billing_document_identifier": "<string>",
